newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas opens higher, then slips with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas opens higher, then slips with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures opened higher, then slipped by midday Wednesday in sluggish trade, with prices still stuck in recent ranges amid little conviction about market direction, industry sources said.
At 1230 EDT, July eased 0.2 cent to $2.12 per million British thermal units after stalling at $2.155. August was 1.5 cents lower at $2.14. Most others also were down slightly.

"There have been a lot of nukes coming back and there's no demand, so it's real tough to get a rally going," said one Texas-based trader, noting heat this week in the Midwest and Northeast was expected to be short-lived.

Traders said the lack of sustained heat and expectations for a sizeable weekly stock build tonight helped undermine sentiment near-term. But few expected the market to collapse, with spreads still favoring up front buying and summer still ahead.
"Everyone's looking for a pretty big storage number, but I think there are a lot of people waiting to buy ahead of $2," said another Texas trader, noting it was too early to be an aggressive bear.
Injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report range from 80 bcf to 110 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks gained 88 bcf.
Forecasts call for more seasonal weather in the Midwest and Northeast by the weekend and into next week. The Southeast was expected to be mostly normal, with Florida climbing to above-normal levels.

Technical traders said recent declines in volume reveal the lack of conviction among players, which has held prices in the same range for almost two weeks. July support was still seen at $2.10, with stronger buying expected at $2.08 and $2. Resistance was pegged first at $2.21, then at $2.25, $2.37 and the contract high at $2.44.

In the cash, swing gas in the Louisiana Gulf was steady early, then slipped a couple of cents to the low-teens. Midcontinent pipes were unchanged in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also held steady in the low-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 13,224 contracts traded at 1150 EDT. Hub open interest on June 10 fell 243 contracts to 196,340.
On the KCBT, July fell 2.5 cents to $1.96, while deferreds were mixed. The East/West spread widened by 2.3 cents to 16.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT open interest on June 10 rose 113 lots to 2,643.
